[Spoiler=Monsters and creatures of Chimú mythology][b]Mythological creatures[/b]
Many creatures are mentioned in Chimú mythology, monsters, which vary from either monstrous versions of a same animal, to i] Apû-Sáman, lord of mountains, who keep the mountains from not collapsing, once, Kùtur, a Amáru with body of serpent and scales of snake, head of cougar with teeth of crocodile, and wings of condor and a tail of crocodile, tried to attack the Lord of Mountains, so it could reach the Chomuñapû top, where the gods live, but the lord of mountains , Apû-Sáman discovered, and then crushed his own weight over the creature (he crushed the Amáru with the mountains ), the place where Kùtur was crushed, is today called Kùturapû.
Some say that who dares enter the caves of Kùturapû, can still hear Kùtur's screams and moans of pain. creature is Kátabân, which has crocodile scales, a llama head, and fox nose, Kátabân is the guardian of the gods mountain, ensuring no mortal will ever cross there, the reason this Amáru emerged from the mountains and showed friendship with the gods is however, unknown.
[i]The Amárus are creatures that even gods are afraid of, and when Taycanamo faced one emerging from the seas, the gods were afraid he would not be capable of crossing the Wichansao, but he surprised even the gods, by using his Ñan and a harpoon, he pierced it left eye, the creature did not retreated, and spit it poison on Taycanamo, but his Ñan, in a sacrificial form, protected him, and saved his life, enraged, Taycanamo swimmed to the creature tail, grabbing it he pierced it scales with a handmade spear, and run over the creature's back while  cutting it, the creature fall dead, and even the  gods were surprised, no god ever killed a Amáru, but a mortal did.[/i]
The other myth about the death of an Amáru is the following:
[i]Chaska, god of strenght, one of the first kids of Chatay and Chilla, his body was like a Ukúchû, robust and strong, despite his warnings to not go to  the Fárapû, due the fact a creature with "body of snake, spit fire, has a cougar head with snake teeth and condor wings" could fight him, and no god killed that creature, only a mortal, but this only made young Chaska more excited, with a mace in hands, he moved to the mountains, his "jumps" over the Fárapû made it "spiky" tips.
As soon Chaska arrived, the thing emmerged from the mountain, spitting fire, in a quick movement, with his agile cougar body, he dodged the fire, and soon the creature rushed at him, Chaska mounted on it back and hit it with his mace on the Amáru's spine 0 paralizying it, the creature died, and it body formed a new chain continuing the Fárapû further north of the mountains.
[
b]Ñan[/b]: A bird bigger and larger than a Condor, with red-yellow vivid feathers, and a tail of fire, it feeds itself with metals such as gold, it caves are filled with such precious metals, those who follow them to their nests can get either death, or wealth.
The few who can domesticate a Ñan, examples include Taycanamo, can have the bird loyal to it owner until death.
[i]Môyco(god of animals) and Sansácun(goddess of fire), Moyco was the first partner of Sansácun, and this marriage led to the ñan, creatures with sharp red-yellow bright feathers and a tail of fire, spitting fire, the Ñans are agressive to any human who approaches, but those who can give them pieces of gold, silver or anything bright to it, will be friendly, Taycanamo domesticated his Ñan by using a pearl.[/i]
[b]Bìrichây:[/b]A monstrous coyote existing around the city of Patítì, it existed at the forests north of the city, it had a "thick brown fur and a roar that paralises those who approach, Taycanamo was tasked to kill this dog and bring it head to the bhapac of the city, Bhátîti, and so he did, with a copper knife, he cut the animal's head and used it fur during the crossing of Wichansao.
[b]Châywakágà[/b]: A enormous whale, with "skin of stone" and sharp teeth, it was another monster, tasked by the gods for Taycanamo kill it, and [i]do a favor[/i] for all coastal communities and cities on the area.
By using a rope, called Guángàma and tie it to a sharp bone, the "Gùtikágà", or whales-killer was a harpoon he made to kill the whale, and cut it skin, he was however, eaten, and when in the animal's mouth, he cut all it interior, making the whale bleed to death, after dragging it to the coast, his mission was considered "complete".
[b]Aypáchek[/b]: A monster in many fishermen histories, with a mouth full of sharp teeth and many tentacles "strong to sink a entire ship", living in the deep ocean, but at full Moon lights, the "moonlight" wakes up the creature, which emerges from the deepth of sea to sink ships and destroy anyone who dares move on sea at the time.
Many histories affirms that Aypáchek is actually a creation of Samanteman, who with his last forces made this giant creature in order to cause max destruction it could, as a reveange for what his brother did to him.

[b]Cíkir[/b]: Another dog, now, the Cíkires are actually a specie of spirits, they live in plains, hunting and attacking those who dare pass there, attacking caravans.
The Cíkires are  believed to be the spirit of caravan dogs that were abandoned in the plains, Wápìwan allowed them to live and search for their owners, so they could rest in peace, those Cíkir who found a caravan which is not theirs, are just attacked brutally.
To escape a cíkir attack , you **must** yell at it the following:
he is not here, search in another one please and let us live.
Do it as much time as necessary until the spirit is gone, no matter how much pain you fell in your throat, keep yelling and it will go away, this is the only way you can escape a cíkir.
b]Chî[/b]: Evil spirits sent away from Sùpâchó, there is mentioned to be only 3 Chîs existing, said to be souls of people so cruel that even Sùpay, the devil itself, feel disgusted by such people, and rejected them, then the Chî surged, shadows who move quickly on corner of your eyes, they can attack anywhere anytime, nothing can kill s Chî, but a amulet of silver can stun them.
Those who are alone at streets or lonely places are their preferred targets,but as it was said , the Chîs can attack anyone, at any place, anytime , either under daylight or night, but they prefer day, the Moonlight and silver (both symbols of goddess Chilla) are make him slower and disorientated .
He makes his presence by whistling, the closer the sound, the more far he is from you, the more far away the sound is, the closer the chî is from you , he attacks by attacking the person with his claws, opening their skin and eating their fat, while other versions mention he bite and sucks the person's fat.
Some variations are on the Chîs appearance, they are mentioned sometimes as man in a black tuxedo wearing gloves, when he takes off his gloves, his claws are shown, in other versions he is represented as a skinny man in common, slightly fancier outfits, but red eyes, other versions are against the ideas of them being rejected by Sùpay , and believe that the Chî are servants of Sùpay to serve him on bringing chaos to the world.
[b]Kóyllûrchá[/b]: a Gigantic shark with crab claws instead of fins.
In response if fishermen killing gravid sharks, Muyvery, the goddess of sea creatures, made the Kóyllûrchá, the spirit of killed gravid sharks who chase ships for 7 days without stopping , tearing the ship's hull until it sinks.
There is no way someone can escape this creature, other than reaching the coast as soon as possible.
[b]Chûspì[/b]: shoals of skeletal fish with teeth sharp enough to destroy a ship's hull when in large numbers.
Those fishermen who adored Samantemán as the true God of seas, had their spirits captured by Cochanamo, who transformed them into skeletal fish who hunt down any ship or living thing that approached them.
The pirate Kûchumì in order to escape a shoal of chûspì landed in Mùynâmowámpà, the island said to be lair of Muyvery and Cochanamo, he stole a beautiful shell from the beach of the island, and indeed, did escaped the fish by sang a melody with the shell, but he kept the shell for himself,  furious because a mortal stole a shell from his island, Cochanamo punished Kûchumì's [b]entire [/b] crew to become a shoal of chûspì.
[b]Mûybîkin[/b]: a colossal crab , one of the creations of Muyvery, it resides in Wichansao strait, and guard it , ensuring no one will enter or leave it, however, those who need pass through, must bring several coins of silver and gold, and give to the Mûybîkin, if it is asleep, then pass silently, without any light on the ship, do not awake it otherwise it will destroy your ship by using it claws.
[b]Káyur[/b]: a beautiful woman, rejected daughter of Cochanammo and Muyvery, she has a body half fish, half woman, with a deformed face, but a impeccable Beautiflul voice, those who reach her are drowned, she takes the mariner head off, and make his skull into a collar for her.
In order to escape her, fishermen bring  hair combs with them to offer to Káyur, as she is obsessed with her own hair.
[b] Chillakágà [/b]: the Whale of Chilla, is a whale with silver skin and a beautiful sing, the mythology mentions two of them, who guard where Samantemán is imprisoned, those who dare reach where he is, face the whales will make enormous waves to sink the ship.
One Chillakágà was once sent by Chilla to sink Wíchàtì, the city of Waves, it Inhabitants did not adore the gods, but monsters, a Chillakágà, which name was "Chaywíchà" or monster of Waves, was sent by Chilla to destroy the city, with a powerful wave made by it tail, the city sunk, and was destroyed, with it entire population being drowned.
The only way to escale a Chillakágà is prevent moving wherever Samantemán is imprisoned, if you reach this and hear a whale sing followed by a massive sound of something moving from the deep sea to surface, move out immediately from where you are, there is no way you can escape a Chillakágà.
[b]Muycùy[/b]: Dark fur cuys, creations of Sùpay, they live in small holes and attack more rural families,  by stealing their kid's voices.
In order to escape a Muycùy, the parents of the kid should leave the kid with something of silver in the kid, many times, either bracelets, or collars of silver.
[b]Wìnkûl[/b]: a deer with obsidian horns and black fur, born from Moyco tears, where both gods, Moyco and Wápìwan had a passion, but neither could ever love each other, the Wìnkûl acts as guardian of Wápítî, ensuring no one will escape it, the Wìnkûl cut the one who tries escape the realm of the dead with It horns, causing them pain , forcing the "escaper" to get back to Wápítî.
No way of escape it, unless you turn around before it attacks you.
[b]Muychárós[/b]: a people that live in Chûgatî, the western country, a people with large hands alongside hairy body , but lacking in stature, said to be creations of Apû-Sáman, the Muychárós created their cities inside the Chûgapû/western mountains, rich in gold and silver, the Muychárós adored Apû-Sáman, and are said to be born from the mountains or stone.
[b]Sàchas[/b]: tree people, some versions call them people that lived on trees, other that they were actual trees , all myths about them mention as they lived in tribes coexisting with nature in  a area called Sàchatî adoring Camác.
Môywánar: a cougar with dark pelt and eyes of fire, it pelt is dark as shadow and it can appear anywhere in the shadow of trees, surged as a punishment from Camác for those who take down trees and destroy nature, the only way to escape this creature is to, when take a down a tree, bring a seed to re-plant what you took down.
[b]Chámórày[/b]: spirit of  bad people that were left by Wápìwan to wander infinitely over Sùpâchó to find Pâkatwan, which they never will found, those who wander through Sùpâchó at night have severe chance to encounter a Chámórày and be imprisoned in the forest and become one of them, they are slow and their cries of melancholy can be heard from distance, making easy to escape, if you are surrounded by them or end up meeting one, without having anything of silver, like a collar or bracelet, or even something of Gold, you are lost, those who have silver and gold with them are protected from the devil spirits.
Súyàman: spirits cursed by Sùpay, servants of him, sometimes sent to the countryside or forests outside Sùpâchó, luring out people at night , lost or not in isolated places by using familiar voices to lure them to a trap, where they are captured and sent to Sùpay becoming one more of his servants, they can imitate human voice and as well as appearance, but not perfectly, their voice is slightly hoarse and not so human, and their body havesome strange aura that can not be descript , but can be recognized .
Just ignore their voice , they will eventually give up, if you meet one of them, do not run, instead stab them with a knife of silver or shoot with bullets of silver, anything of silver works if thrown at them.
[b]Atúkí[/b]: a Gigantic spider that exists inside of caves, those who dare enter the caves will encounter them, they  After catching their prey, the Atúkís spin their webs, trapping people, after the person is killed, they put their eggs inside the person, after hatching,  the small spiders will eat the person from inside.
They were a creation of Apû-Sáman for those who dare enter the caves without his permission, when encounter a Atúkí, she will say the following:
What are the pass words?
After that, you must do the [I] pray of the mountains[/I].
Which is the following:
Apû-Sáman, Ykóchapû y apûban yáy,  yágû tachày.
Apû-Sáman , ykíichá chaskí iáwaku  úswayllá sùpach.
Apû-Sáman, sáman Ykóchapû y apûban, Ñoganchikánbe
Translation:
Apû-Sáman, mountains and caves father, hear pray of mine.
Apû-Sáman , your strength protect us from falling the darkness .
Apû-Sáman  , lord of caves and mountains, we praise you[/I]
After such pray, the atúkí will allow you to enter the caves.
[b]Kárapûn[/b]: a snake that inhabits volcanoes, Creations of Sákapû(goddess of volcanoes).
Kárapûns are not aggressive, were created as a warning from Sákapû to evacuate cities or people living next to volcanoes when one was going to erupt, Kárapûns are not aggressive, despite their large obsidian bodies, they warn humans living next to volcanoes that a eruption will happen, they warn one week before eruptions happen.
Tikúrrày: a monstrous armadillothat did existed, when chimu farmers discovered bones of such creature around 1020, many myths about a monstrous armadillo began to surge.
It is said to be a second age being , giant animals  made by Kón and Camác, when Samanteman dried  the world, the Tikúrrày digged depth in Erene to found water, but never did, and were trapped inside Camác, some believe that when Erenequakes happens, and bones of Tikúrrày bones are close, it is them demanding water, in order to calm them down, offer them water by throwing water digging until you found their bones and throw the water at them.
There is no other known way to calm them down, if not thrown water, they will keep doing Erenequakes until calmed down , that is why many water wells are made to ensure they will never be thirsty.
[b]Yácha and Kûnsù:[/b] two condors of Sùpay, acting as his eyes ,  yácha act as his eyes on Sùpâchó, observing everything and everyone on Sùpâchó, while Kûnsù is his eyes on Erene, watching carefully everything and everyone where his domain in the human world, which is said to be what those who adore Sùpay see and anywhere they are in.
Example : one adorer of Sùpay that lives in a neighborhood of Chanchán, Kûnsù can see, and consequently Sùpay, everything about the neighborhood the adorer lives, houses with silver or people wearing something of silver however, can not be seen and are invisible to Kûnsù, that is why most houses of Chancháns centre have details of silver on their doors borders, and many nobles, governors and the Sapa use Silver earrings, which are also commonly sold at stores.
Kónsùpa: a darkness grotesque creature, made by Supay to mock Kón, it has a deformed feline body, it was the spirit of a person known for lying, and Sùpay made it appear on the shadows and dark alleys of great cities, but also feed itself by lies, pray, that is the only way to escape it, but if you have no faith, the creature will laugh at you and say you have religion, but no faith, and will kill the person, this is for those who encounter it on the alleys, those who lies and are persecuted and encounter it, in order to escape, must yell a painful truth about them, such act will make the Kónsùpa vanish.
[b]Llákumú[/b]: bioluminescent shells that create in sank ships, created by Cochanamo to punish those who sack sack sank ships treasures, those who see it light are hypnotized and try steal it pearl, but as soon the sacker touches the pearl, their memories vanish, and die drowned for forgetting how swim back to surface, the Llákumú pearl hides everyone who touched it, their memories, do not enter sank ships with open eyes, so the Llákumú light will not hypnotize you.
Ókallay: a carnivorous plant made by Sùpay, cursing the vegetation of Sùpâchó, those who enter the forest, can smell it attractive smell, as if controlled to follow right where the plants are , and then, eaten by the plant, to escape, cover your nose and run, run as fast as you can, you can not save yourself when you feel your legs going against your will to move towards the good smell
